athlete.name: Lucy Kesler
athlete.bio: A tenacious playmaker with a keen tactical mind, she thrives in orchestrating attacks. Off the field, her infectious enthusiasm and dedication inspire teammates, embodying a spirit of relentless pursuit and camaraderie.

caption:
Meet Lucy Kesler!

“Hi, I’m Lucy! I’ve been in love with the game of soccer since I was five, back when I was doing more cartwheels on the field than kicking the ball. Today I play in the midfield, where I use my left foot, vision, and work rate to connect the game, and build the attack. What drives me most is using soccer to inspire others to dream big and stay focused forward. I’m a big sister, a dog lover, a slalom skier, and my faith shapes everything I do on and off the field.
As Secretary of SAAC, I work alongside student-athletes across campus and the Big 12 to strengthen leadership, service, and community. I’ve also loved mentoring younger athletes...from working with kids with intellectual and developmental disabilities to leading my mentorship program for high school girls navigating soccer and the college recruiting process. After BYU, I hope to play professional soccer and pursue a career in sports law so I can continue advocating for athletes!”

#byu #gocougs #womenssoccer #collegesoccer #soccer

athlete.name: Dalton Mortensen
athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor with a knack for strategic play, this athlete thrives under pressure. Known for his infectious enthusiasm and unwavering work ethic, he elevates teammates and leaves a lasting impact on the game.

caption:
Mini taper?
This is important for any athlete who’s racing more than once or twice in a season! Which is to say almost every distance runner. You can’t do a full taper every other week, all season long, and still expect to make fitness gains.
So how can you get to the line feeling fresh, without tapering all the way as if it’s the last race of the season? The short answer is: train through race weeks, but with a mini taper.
It’s the same principle as tapering for a championship, but shorter time frame. So it might start 3-4 days out from a race, rather than a week or more. 
This means you can still have a solid workout 3-4 days out, and then start a mini taper the next day. Mileage drops for the next 3 days leading up to the race, and do some strides to stay sharp.
Keeping enough intensity on race week is key to a good taper, as long as it’s not adding fatigue that will last more than a day or two.
This isn’t one-size-fits-all, but it’s my best general advice!

caption:
Meet Ellie Walbruch!

“Soccer has always been part of my life. I grew up in a super competitive, athletic family! Both of my parents played Division I sports, my brother plays on the BYU men’s soccer team, my little sister is also a BYU student, and my youngest sister is following right behind as a soccer player. Competing and supporting each other has always been our normal.
From a young age, I knew I wanted to play at the highest level possible. All the sacrifices led me to BYU, where I get to compete, grow, and chase big goals every day. Being part of BYU athletics has shaped me not only as a player, but as a person!! 
After graduating, I hope to play professional soccer and eventually step into sports media as a sideline reporter, staying close to sports which I love! Grateful for this journey and proud to represent BYU. GO COUGS 💙💙”

caption:
Weekend recovery tips!
1. Train easy and rest! I recommend taking 1 full day with either very little or no training. For me this is always on Sundays!
2. Eat! Keep fueling your body with plenty of carbs, protein, and fats. Your body needs energy to repair itself and adapt to the training. Don’t use a rest day as a reason to skip meals. 
3. Sleep more! Sounds like a no-brainer, but you’d be surprised by how many people get less sleep on weekends rather than more. Try to keep your bedtime the same, and add a nap if you can!

caption:
We had the pleasure of preparing @mackenzee_vance for her first professional season with @tuzasoficial ⚽️

Our main goal with Mackenzee was to prepare her for the demands she was going to ultimately be exposed to in pre-season camp. Her training program focused heavily on tissue tolerance of the lower leg, acceleration, change of direction/deceleration, power and conditioning.

Soccer players want to go into pre-season feeling as fit as possible, so when it comes to conditioning we tend to get more specific. This is where we prescribe more intensive aerobic power work and lactic explosive repeats (shown) in the means to mirror the energy system demands from the game as much as possible. We also like to add the ball during their active rest periods, as this allows them to get on a ball while fatigued. 

Goodluck Mac! 💪

#opzoneutah #coach #sportsperformance #strength #athlete #utahstrengthcoach

athlete.name: Stone Cushing
athlete.bio: With a fierce determination and a crafty repertoire, this right-handed pitcher blends precision with power. Hailing from a small town, he thrives on competition and embraces challenges with unwavering confidence.

caption:
Time is a funny thing. Sometimes it feels like it’s not moving at all and sometimes you can’t seem to get it to slow down. It’s been around 8 months since my baseball career came to an end, and over that time I was able to feel my true emotions, heal myself, and find an understanding of the way this world works and the things that matter the most in life.

Baseball teaches a lot of lessons, and as I approach the first opening day of my life that I’m not currently training for, I feel compelled to share one with the next generation of not only baseball players, but people. Take advantage of every opportunity to make yourself better. Whether that’s on the field, in your career, in your personal relationships, etc. Put in work. Don’t cheat yourself. Prioritize your mental health. The one thing in the future that can get you by when nothing else will is the thought and belief that you gave it everything you had. Nobody can take that away from you, and I’ve made that reflection about my own career. I truly put my heart and soul into this game, and I hope that I can pass on some of the knowledge I gained in my experiences to those of you I come in contact with.

Change is scary, the unknown is scary, but with the support of my perfect wife Chloe I know that we will thrive through every stage of life, and I can’t wait. I appreciate my family, friends, and all those who have impacted my life positively to this point. The best is yet to come. 💪

Video was made by @robertphilpotlll who is a wizard at what he does!

athlete.name: Emma Barbero
athlete.bio: Known for her tenacity and keen court awareness, this fearless libero transforms defense into art, effortlessly reading opponents' moves. Off the court, her infectious enthusiasm inspires teammates, fueling a vibrant team spirit.

caption:
Meet Emma Barbero!

“I’m from Asti, Italy and I have an older sister, Sofia. She was my example when I was young so I was following all her decisions about what sport we were choosing. Before playing volleyball we were doing horse riding, then we decided to start playing volleyball when I was 10 years old. Volleyball was only a fun game at first, but soon it became my passion and I started dreaming big, I wanted to play one day for the national team and the pro league in Italy. The club wasn’t close to my home, so the only way to go play for that team was to leave my house and my parents and go live with other teammates. I was only 12 years old when I made that decision and I immediately accepted it. My parents let me completely free to choose what I wanted and they gave me all their support, I’m not taking that for granted and I’m so grateful for them. 
During those years I also achieved my dream to play with the national team, playing the European championship and the World championship and won the “best libero” in both competitions. After high school I got a call to play in the pro league, so my last year in Italy I was playing for the Megabox Vallefoglia, sharing the locker room with some Olympic players. Volleyball hasn’t been my whole priority during my life, school and my instruction were equally important. Playing pro and having practice every morning and afternoon couldn’t allow me to study at university so I decided to move across the world and come to college in the USA.
It’s another dream that comes true. Even if it’s not only easy to stay away from my family for a long long stay, I’m making a lot of lifelong experiences, learning a new language, making so many friends all over the word and living my best life. I’m currently studying microbiology and in the future I’d like to work in a laboratory, doing research and working every day with these little funny microbes. Next year I’ll be a senior, after that I still have to decide if I wanna go play pro somewhere in the world or start my new career but volleyball allowed me this crazy beautiful life and will be always part of me forever!”

athlete.name: Dalton Mortensen
athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor with a knack for strategic play, this athlete thrives under pressure. Known for his infectious enthusiasm and unwavering work ethic, he elevates teammates and leaves a lasting impact on the game.

caption:
1. I feel more fresh for workouts so I get more out of them! When you prioritize feeling good for faster sessions, you have better workouts and that builds confidence. Workouts are also a much better indicator of race potential than just mileage. 

2. Mileage is a means to an end, not an end in itself. It’s also very subjective, and everyone’s body responds slightly differently to the same training. I can usually handle more running volume, but the workouts suffer if I run too much. Finding what’s best for your body can take some trial and error, and it can change over time!

3. Indoor track means no 10,000m. So my priority shifts improving my 3k and 5k racing! Mastering the shorter distances will pay dividends in your running career.

Years ago, my parents taught me the importance of having a vision of where you want to go, setting goals aligned with the vision, and making specific plans to accomplish them. 

As I think about where I want to go in this upcoming year, it’s important to remember where I’ve been, remember what I’ve learned, and remember how I’ve grown.

After lots of prayer and fasting over the past two weeks, I’m super excited to announce my commitment to play soccer at Texas Tech University! ❤️🖤

I’m so grateful for my faith and my Savior Jesus Christ. He has guided and directed every step of my journey, even when things were hard or I didn’t know which direction to take. He has shown me—over and over—that “all these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good.” I’ve felt His hand leading me, shaping me, and preparing me for this opportunity.

Lubbock already feels like home. I was blown away by the amazing campus and the Texas Tech pride that fills the city. I can’t wait to give everything I have to this place and work every single day to make y’all proud.

I’m also so grateful for everyone at BYU who supported me and helped me grow into the player and person I am today. Your love means the world. 

To the Texas Tech staff — thank you for believing in me and giving me the chance to write this new chapter. I won’t take a single day for granted.

I’m fired up, grateful, and ready to get to work. God opened this door, and I’m walking through it with faith and everything I’ve got.

He coordinates the BYU Pathway Program, mentoring students across Africa and the South Pacific to strengthen English skills and prepare for internships and jobs. Through weekly Zoom sessions, he supports students with resume building, interview strategies, AI training, and more. As Service Committee Co-Chair of BYU’s Student-Athlete Advisory Committee, he organized Christmas tree deliveries and donation drives for refugee centers. Wall also traveled to Israel, leading youth camps and community clean-ups. Wall spoke at an elementary school literacy event, sharing his early struggles with reading and encouraging students to embrace growth and resilience. Join us in honoring Tanner’s commitment to community service!

athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor with an eye for strategy, she weaves through defenses like a maestro conducting a symphony. Off the field, her infectious enthusiasm inspires teammates and fans alike.

caption:
“There’s something about running that lets me test myself in a way nothing else does. You get to feel your body fight for every second, every rep, every mile, and that struggle feels empowering. Running gives you a place to be bold and to show up tired, sore, unsure, and choose to push anyway. These perspectives can allow for a moment where things click and you realize you just blew past a limit you thought was real. It gives you this confidence that says, “I can do this.” 

Running has also connected me with incredible people such as teammates who understand, coaches who have high expectations and competitors who constantly raise the level. The miles can be messy and hurt at times, but that’s the beauty of it. Running teaches you and gives you the opportunity to choose how you want to show up in hard moments. It allows for greater self discovery and gives you a chance to continue to evolve.”

These are the miles that made #GarminSponsoredAthlete @janehedengren

📸 @alyssadahneke

caption:
Being at BYU has been one of the greatest blessings of my life. This place has shaped me, stretched me, and taught me more about myself than I ever expected. I’ve experienced some of my highest highs here and some of my lowest lows — but through it all, one truth has stayed constant: I am a daughter of God, and He has walked with me every step of the way.

I’m forever grateful for the time I had to wear BYU across my chest and be a Cougar. Thank you to my teammates, coaches, and everyone who poured into me these last two years. BYU will always have a piece of my heart. Go Cougs!! 💙

With that said, I’m excited for a new chapter. I can’t wait to take my love for the game somewhere new, grow into the player and person I know I can be, and show what I’m capable of. Here’s to new beginnings and trusting in Gods plan for me.  #transferring

athlete.name: Cate Phipps Louis
athlete.bio: With a fierce competitive spirit and unwavering determination, this sprinter combines speed and agility to dominate the track. A relentless work ethic fuels her pursuit of excellence, inspiring teammates and fans alike.

caption:
this year, learning to be grateful in the moment changed my life. here are just some of the times i was completely overwhelmed with gratitude:

1 - we are now real adults with real jobs in the real world with our big goals and dreams. i’m so grateful for alema’s relentless support, sacrifice, and love. he inspires me to be better every day. 
2 - feb 1: i (pretty much) ran my first top 10 time for BYU. i am not the kind of person to be frustrated that i barely made number 10. i know how far i’ve come and what a privilege from God i’d been given. 
3 - feb 14: i had the best track meet i’ve ever had with the best teammates i’ve ever had. to see their success and be counted among them was an honor to me
4 - april 24: alema and i graduated! i am so grateful to live in a time and place where women can get any education they choose. i grew spiritually and intellectually through my BYU education. Elder Uchtdorf, whose teachings on hope got me through my hardest days, spoke at the ceremony. 
5 - april 26: i ran my fastest ever 100 and 200 with my parents watching, and i did it alongside two women i deeply admire and love. while i waited for my heat, i felt so much peace and gratitude
6 - may 1: we ran our best 4x4 ever and solidified our spot for regionals, even with no one to compete against. this video still makes my heart beat fast. i am so grateful for teammates who embraced me as i was. with them, i achieved so much more than i ever would have on my own.
7 - may 17: i ran my last individual collegiate race at Big 12s. the outcome and conditions were disappointing, but it was overpowered by gratitude for how far i’d come and how blessed i’d been
8 - may 31: we ran at regionals. i owe so much to this 4x4 team. although my dream of going to nationals was unfulfilled, my heart was full and my tears were in gratitude—i had already lived my dream for 4 years.
9-12 - the 7 days after regionals were exhausting in every way, as i (with MUCH help) packed to move, got my torn labrum diagnosis, crammed for the CSCS, and more. i am so thankful for every friend who helped me, laughed with me, danced with me, and drove with me. it means more than i can explain. 
(rest in comments)

What a comeback season for @elliewalbruch ⚡️

This was Ellie’s first season back after suffering an ACL injury back in the spring of 2024. The statistics surrounding ACL reconstructions are quite astonishing. Only about 50% of athletes that suffer an ACL injury return to their pre-injury levels and of those who do return roughly 25% of them will suffer a second ACL injury to the same or opposite knee. That number is even higher if the athlete returns before 9 months.

With Ellie, because of her longer training history we had pre-injury data, which helped guide her return to play process. Her achievements this season showed that she is back and even performing better than her pre-injury levels. To name a few:

•Second Team All-American
•All Big 12 First Team
•Big 12 Tournament Offensive Player MVP
•16 Goals
•Big 12 Tournament Champ
•NCAA Sweet 16 Appearance

Most importantly she stayed injury free, which allowed her to start all 24 games this season. This goes to show how effective a proper ACL rehab program, if executed well can be.

It’s time to hang up the cap and goggles💙

Transferring to BYU after my freshman year at Arkansas, I pictured the next chapter of my swim career. Instead it became a long battle with injuries. Last season I medically redshirted, holding onto hope that this year I’d return to the pool. But once again I stayed out of the water. More doctors. More MRIs. More uncertainty.

I’ve now been told I need a career-ending surgery.

A small part of me feels relief in finally having answers. A much bigger part of me feels completely lost. After dedicating 15 years to this sport, losing it like this was never something I had pictured. Swimming shaped me in how I work, how I dream, how I push, and who I’ve become outside the pool too.

I’m incredibly grateful for everything this sport gave me: the opportunities, the exciting travels, and all the people who became part of me along the way.

To my teammates from club, high school, and college swim, thank you for being my family. You make the tough days easier and the great days unforgettable. You filled this journey with so much love.

To my parents, thank you for every sacrifice, every meet in the stands, every early morning drive, and every comeback you supported me through. I could never have done this without you.

To all my coaches throughout the years, thank you. Whether you taught me the basics or pushed me toward bigger goals, every correction and piece of encouragement built the athlete and person I am today.

Coach Franks and Coach Peeps, thank you for seeing beyond the swimmer. You believed in when I didn’t and helped me grow far past the sport itself. The confidence, strength, and self-belief you helped me find will stay with me long after the pool.

A special thank you to Coach Tamber, who gave me the chance to come home to BYU. For the grace, trust, and constant encouragement. Though this ending wasn’t part of the plan, your continuous support means more than you’ll ever know.

This wasn’t the ending I pictured. But I’m choosing gratitude over bitterness. The journey over the heartbreak.

Swimming gave me more than I could ever give back. And for that, I will always be thankful. Now onto that swammer life.

caption: Setting! Good mechanics are important, but so is good vision. In this video, 2-time Olympic medalist Courtney Thompson @cthomp_3 and BYU setter Alex Bower @alex.bowerr show us the eyework process a setter should go through in serve-receive. 1st) Setters should look at the server to get some cues about where the serve might be going. 2nd) Setters should watch the serve and be prepared to make a play on a short serve if necessary. 3rd) When seeing where the serve is going, setters should immediately turn to the soon-to-be passer and watch the passer's platform to get some cues about where the pass might be going. Setters should be in an athletic, comfortable posture throughout this process. For more, get started for free on GMS+ by clicking the link in the bio. #volleyball #coaching #highschool #club #college #ncaa #byu #big12 #usa #setting #fundamentals #vision #eyework #gmsplus #goldmedalsquared

athlete.name: Paiton Collins
athlete.bio: A tenacious guardian of the net, her quick reflexes and sharp instincts captivate fans. With a fierce determination and a calming presence, she inspires teammates while fearlessly thwarting opponents' advances.

caption:
Sophomore year looked nothing like I expected. I earned my starting spot and played 1,543 minutes, I ended my season with a complete ACL tear, MCL, meniscus, and a fractured femur. 

For a long time I was sad, angry, and couldn’t understand why this would happen to me. Today I’m 2 1/2 weeks post op, and although I still have moments of uncertainty and grief, I’m healing one day at a time. This is just a chapter, not the whole story.

I’ll see south field next year!!!!

athlete.bio: A tenacious forward with a fierce competitive spirit, she skillfully navigates defenders, blending creativity and precision. Off the field, her infectious enthusiasm inspires teammates, making every practice a memorable experience.

caption:
season of highs, lows, and the biggest comeback of my life 🤍 fought my way back from ACL injury and ended up living out everything I prayed for. this team never stopped believing…in the grind, in our goals, and, most importantly, in each other.
there are truly no words to describe what this year has meant to me. there is no place like BYU. a program that feels like home in every way. teammates who are my best friends and coaches who believed & cared about us day in and day out.
big wins, big accomplishments…BIG 12 CHAMPS & SWEET 16 QUALIFIERS! 
soccer & competing has always been my greatest teacher in life.. showing me how to work, how to believe, and how to rise, even when it’s hard.
my heart is so full of gratitude. grateful for my team, grateful for BYU, for MY journey, and for every moment this season that reminded me why I fought so hard to come back 💙
now back to work!

athlete.name: Kylie Mantz
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with an unyielding spirit, this distance runner thrives on pushing boundaries. Fueled by passion and resilience, she embodies dedication, inspiring teammates with her unwavering focus and infectious enthusiasm.

caption:
🗣️ “You need to experience it to have respect for it and the emotional waves you go through during it”

For @kyliehmantz, her 2:43:49 win at the Two Cities Marathon wasn’t just a fast time for her first-ever marathon but also a lived crash course on what it means to take on 26.2, staying in it when the legs go heavy and to keep@moving when “stopping is not an option.”

What makes her journey so compelling is how quickly everything has unfolded: from barely racing in high school to starting to run to try and understand @connermantz’s world and career. She quickly realized she belonged in it from walking onto the @byutrackfieldxc to eventually finding the confidence to chase the U.S. Olympic Marathon Trials qualifying standard.

Unconventional, yes. But also incredibly relatable. Her path is proof that you can start late, dream big and still surprise yourself.

🎧 Stream, download and listen to her full interview on The CITIUS MAG Podcast via Apple Podcasts, Spotify or wherever you get your shows.

athlete.name: Kylie Mantz
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with an unyielding spirit, this distance runner thrives on pushing boundaries. Fueled by passion and resilience, she embodies dedication, inspiring teammates with her unwavering focus and infectious enthusiasm.

caption:
✨Marathon Debut and a win!✨

Thanks @2citiesmarathon for an incredible race this past weekend! I was told your first marathon has a special kind of magic to it. You only run your first marathon once - embrace it! I’ll be honest while it was a great experience, I made a lot of “first marathon” mistakes (go read my Strava recap of it if you want details😂). I walked away hitting some of my goals, but far from all of them. I left Fresno humbled and grateful…but hungry for improvement🤪. 

I felt privileged I had the chance to run my first marathon in my home town. While training I’d picture myself running the streets I know I’d run in the race. They were streets I grew up using🥹. I had friends, family, community members who came out to cheer, waving silly signs at me (swipe to see some of them😂) I felt supported and loved. Those cheers got me to the finish line🫶🏻. 

There’s really no way to stimulate marathon pain other than actually racing. At one point, I was experiencing a type of pain I had never felt. I turned to Conner - my pacer🥰 - and said “I think I’m done. It’s too hard.” He looked back at me and said, “stopping’s not an option. You can slow down, but you can’t stop. Let’s finish this marathon.” I knew he was right. I dropped my expectations and focused on finishing strong. Putting one foot in front of the other. 

I thought about what Conner said and the power that statement had: just. don’t. stop. There are many things in our lives that are hard and our natural instinct is to quit, retreat, hide, rather than push forward, embrace the uncomfortable and vulnerability, and risk failure or disappointment. (Side note: I’d never say this race is a failure or a disappointment!☝🏻). When we choose to keep moving forward, we tap into our potential. Our bodies are capable of much more than what our brains think they can. 

So while I learned the importance of fueling and pacing🫠 the thing I learned the most is to not quit. We’re stronger than we think and when we choose to keep moving, we surprise ourselves by winning in ways we didn’t expect🥇.

🏃‍♂️ Running side-by-side through 26.2 miles

❤️ Balancing love, purpose, and pursuit

✝️ The role of faith in staying grounded

🏆 What it means to become the person you’re meant to be America’s fastest marathoner and his “better half” open up about marriage, mindset, and what it truly means to build something together.

🎧 New episode out now — hit the link in bio and comment “PODCAST” when you’ve listened.

athlete.name: Emma Marusakova
athlete.bio: Versatile swimmer with a flair for freestyle, butterfly, and backstroke, she combines grace and tenacity in the pool. Known for her relentless spirit, she inspires teammates with unwavering positivity and dedication.

caption:
Meet Emma Marušáková, a senior on the BYU Swim and Dive team majoring in Psychology with a minor in Sociology and Family Life! She’s set to graduate in April 2026 and competes in sprint and mid-distance butterfly, backstroke, and freestyle.

Emma is passionate about understanding people and helping children and families build healthier lives. Growing up in Slovakia and now studying in the U.S. has taught her resilience, balance, and the importance of community.

When she’s not swimming, Emma loves reading, cooking, traveling, spending time outdoors, and being with her family, boyfriend, and animals. After graduation, she plans to pursue a master’s degree in Marriage and Family Therapy, where she hopes to combine traditional therapy with animal-assisted approaches to support emotional well-being.

Emma’s biggest piece of advice? Be kind to yourself and others. Stay patient—progress, whether in school, your career, sports, or relationships, takes time. Every small step forward counts. 💙

athlete.name: Kylie Mantz
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with an unyielding spirit, this distance runner thrives on pushing boundaries. Fueled by passion and resilience, she embodies dedication, inspiring teammates with her unwavering focus and infectious enthusiasm.

caption:
Today is our three year anniversary!🤍

My father in law the other day asked, “did you ever imagine yourself living the pro athlete life before getting married?” I laughed, absolutely not! Goodness, what a wild 3 years!

At the start of our marriage, I felt like a deer in the headlights with all things pro running. I didn’t really run let alone do sports HS, had just come home from my mission, had a lot of school left, and knew nothing about contracts, sponsorships, training, and pressure of racing. I’ve had to learn a lot! That might make me sound naive, but I believe it was divine intervention. 

Marriage reveals your strengths and weaknesses. That exposure is vulnerable. There have been several awkward and embarrassing moments in our marriage as I’ve navigated this career while trying to strengthen our relationship. It’s brought me to my knees many times and helping me draw closer to Christ. 

Driving home from the airport the other day after getting home from Chicago, I looked over at Conner (madly trying to answer all of your sweet texts! Again, there have been so many messages. If he doesn’t get to yours, know we really appreciate it!!). I had the word “mantle” come to mind. By definition it means, “an important role or responsibility that passes from one person to another.” What’s the mantle that’s been placed on my shoulders? Supporting, listening, planning, organizing, loving, serving, being steady while chaos is all around, etc. I had many examples of things I’ve done and should do going forward that reflects that mantle on my shoulders. 

I’m far from perfect at this. I’ve had a few breaking points this build haha. There’s no manual to how to support your pro athlete husband😂. 

I’m grateful for a forgiving, caring, and loving husband who recognizes I’m trying. I’m so proud of Conner for of course his performances, but also his quiet, unseen acts of kindness. I’m inspired by him and honored to be his wife! 

Happy anniversary Sweetheart😘

athlete.name: Kylie Mantz
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with an unyielding spirit, this distance runner thrives on pushing boundaries. Fueled by passion and resilience, she embodies dedication, inspiring teammates with her unwavering focus and infectious enthusiasm.

caption:
Our Park City adventures have come to an end. We’re on our way to Chicago! Race day in 4 days🙌🏻. 

Our time in PC has been more of a refining experience than I anticipated. I came up here with my personal plan/timeline for how things were to go in my life post graduation, but learned my plan wasn’t the Lord’s. That realization has been frustrating and confusing. I’ve learned however that God’s not in a rush. He’s not “shooting for the next big thing” like sometimes I do. He’s more invested in our growth and our day to day living. 

Surrounding myself with marathoners has been an eye opening and spiritual experience. These runners aren’t focused on how fast they can run for a short period of time, but how to function running an uncomfortably fast but controlled pace for a LONG time. There’s no quick gratification. From an outsider looking in, it looks boring, mundane, repetitive, and unnecessary levels of exhaustion. From someone invested in the pursuit, it brings purpose, order, patience, diligence, and fulfillment. 

They use two phrases: 
- The “mundanity of excellence” and 
- c^{2} = e^{2} (consistent competent effort equals eventual excellence). 

Small, steady, (sometimes boring and/or hard) things leads to great results. It’s not all at once, it doesn’t require a life changing situation. It’s doing the little things you know are right that compound on each other. 

A lot of us think if I only had a better job, was married, had kids, quit school, retired, etc. we’d be happier. 

Sometimes we have to be okay, (maybe for longer than we thought) to do the mundane things. Just go to work, complete the homework assignment, run the miles, change the dirty diapers, take the kids to practice, read your scriptures, pray, attend church, do your calling, take the medicine, go to therapy, etc. over and over again. Allow the mundane things to compound and build on each other. 

I’ve seen as I’ve focused on doing those small and simple things, great things really have come to pass (Mosiah 2:18:)). My character and perspective have changed dramatically. Thank you PC for your refining experiences.

Now onto Chicago😤

athlete.bio: A relentless force on the field, this offensive lineman combines strength and agility with a strategic mindset. Off the gridiron, a thoughtful leader, fostering camaraderie and resilience among teammates.

caption:
My father has always been a role model in my life, he showed me how to love Christ and to love our families. He taught us to give and not be selfish with what we have while being respectful to everyone . He was truly a God fearing man.

“Blessed are the peacemakers⁠: for they shall be called the children of God.” Matthew 5:9

From taking us to eat, fun trips, to catching my first fish, teaching us to pray every night, showing us to love our brothers even when it’s hard, having fun while doing chores, cooking the best food, making jokes and getting a good laugh. Seeing my dad chase down bears, swim with sharks, among many other crazy things you would think he was invincible and will be around forever. Time with my dad went by too fast and I would love one more trip on the road. There are many many great memories that I will cherish and tell my children.

Rest in peace Dad
07/18/73-9/24/25

athlete.name: Charlie Miska
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a knack for breaking tackles, this powerhouse blends agility and power. Off the field, his infectious enthusiasm and leadership inspire teammates, embodying the spirit of BYU football.

caption:
The Prophet for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Russell M. Nelson, passed away last night. Just as God had prophets who led His people in ancient times, we believe God likewise has a prophet to lead His church on the earth today. 

I can’t express how instrumental he has been to me. Every good thing that has come in my life over the last couple years has been a direct result of following his teachings. 

Here are some of my favorites: 
- True joy comes from our focus on Christ regardless of our circumstances. 
- God wants to speak to us, make time to communicate to Him and Hear Him.
- We are literal children of God.
- Faith in Jesus Christ moves the mountains in our lives. 
- Attend the temple as often as our circumstances permit. Nothing can replace what the temple can do for us.
- Express gratitude daily. It heals and strengthens. 
- Serve a mission. 
- Read the Book of Mormon daily.
- Be a peacemaker. Love your neighbor. Build those around you. 

I’ve experienced the promise God made to those who follow His prophet— “For his word ye shall receive, as if from mine own mouth, in all patience and faith. For by doing these things the gates of hell shall not prevail against you; yea, and the Lord God will disperse the powers of darkness from before you, and cause the heavens to shake for your good⁠, and his name’s glory⁠” (D&C 21:5-6).

Seeing how the prophet’s teachings have influenced my life in these profound ways, 
I will sustain and follow our next prophet, Dallin H. Oaks, with all I got.

athlete.name: Jane Hedengren
athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor with an eye for strategy, she weaves through defenses like a maestro conducting a symphony. Off the field, her infectious enthusiasm inspires teammates and fans alike.

caption:
What a blessing it is to have a body. For the joy and gift it is to be alive, healthy, happy and able to discover those boundaries for the time being. My last HS season is in the books and here’s some things I tried out.

Evaluate your “why” often and center yourself in that. When it get’s tough and you’ve pushed enough for yourself, do it for them. For the people who sacrificed so you could enjoy the privilege. For god, allowing you to have a healthy body and letting your light shine. Whatever it might be, turn outward and lean into that gratitude. 

Like a child, go for it. Don’t trade the magic for a measured hope. There is so much possibility within racing. Where’s the magic in over-analyzing? Maximize that effort, enjoy it, be kind and see what happens. 

Racing allows for self discovery. You can learn a lot about yourself in those few minutes. Who do you want to be? Apply that in racing and be proud of the effort. I hope you can “say yes” to more, time and time again as it gets harder. It’s often worth it. 

This season gave me much to look back on and even more to carry forward. Nike helped me share a bit of that journey in a video about my story. Check out the full film on the @Nike YouTube channel. Link in bio.

caption:
PGA Tour Procore Championship Monday Q- 

I started my round off with a bogey after hitting my tee shot in the trees and being forced to chip out. Midway through my front nine I got hot and made 3 birdies in a row to get to -3. I made the turn and got cold.. I failed to get up and down for birdie on #10 and then made 3 bogeys in a row. I knew the number would be -6 so making the turn I was confident I would continue playing well and shoot the score to get in. I ended up finishing at only -1. Disappointing round, but I still feel like me game is where I want it to be and I am close to breaking out. Thanks for the continued support. See you next week!

Aunque en un primer instante sentí que el mundo se me venía abajo, hoy puedo decir que me llevo aprendizaje, humildad y una motivación más grande que nunca para seguir persiguiendo objetivos ambiciosos. Esto apenas empieza 

Agradezco profundamente a quienes demuestran estar también en los momentos duros, a mi familia, amigos, compañeros, entrenadores y @menteparaganaracademy , a @jaguaresuamnca @evolveatnic, @bonnevillemeats, @MSPLA, , FNA y CON por su apoyo constante al deporte nicaragüense.

Somebody pinch me 🥹

I’ve been preparing her all month for preschool thinking she would have a hard time saying goodbye on her first day. I thought she’d cry lots and lots of tears and want to stay with me forever - only for her to give me a hug and go straight into her classroom. Without even looking back I might add lol 😭

Naisina is everything I want to be when I grow up. Kind. Funny. Adventurous. Full of Hope. Brave. Incredibly forgiving. Confident. She’s a good friend and an even better sister. She breathes new life into every space she walks into. To put it simply, she truly just loves life.

I hate that I’m one step closer to sharing her with the world, but I love that she’s the kind of soul this world needs. 🫶🏽 Who knew PreK prep was so dramatic lol. #RaisingWorldChangers

caption:
To say I’m proud of this girl doesn’t even begin to cover it. Watching Brynn step into this experience has been one of the greatest blessings of my life, greater than anything I could have dreamed of for myself. I never imagined we would get to walk through something this special and yet here we are, living it together.

Brynn has always been more than just my sister, she is my very best friend, my safe place, and the person who makes me laugh the hardest. She’s doing this whole journey her own way, with so much grace, strength, and authenticity, and that makes me even more proud.

She inspires me daily with the way she carries herself, the way she loves people, and the way she is unafraid to be fully and completely Brynn. I’m so lucky to be her sister, and I can’t wait to keep cheering her on every step of the way. Miss Americas Teen here she comes!!

caption:
Hello, Provo!! 
I still can’t believe this is real! I am so incredibly honored to serve as Miss Provo 2025! This year, I can’t wait to share my heart with this community and bring my initiative, Win Within: Advocating for Athletes, to as many people as possible. As a pre-med student at BYU, former collegiate athlete, and lifelong advocate for athlete wellness, I am passionate about helping athletes discover who they are beyond their sport and supporting their mental and physical health.

Huge thanks to my family, friends, and everyone who has supported me — this means the world to me. I’m especially grateful to be on this journey alongside my amazing friend, @elle.amiller sharing this opportunity with someone I admire so much is truly a dream come true! 

If you have an event, school, or team you’d like me to visit — please reach out! I’d love to serve, speak, and connect!

Here’s to a year of service, connection, and making a difference in the city I love! #MissProvo2025 #WinWithin #AdvocatingForAthletes

caption:
Kader komplett! ✅

Die SBB Baskets haben das letzte Puzzleteil für die kommende Saison in der Barmer 2. Basketball-Bundesliga Pro A gefunden: Mit der Verpflichtung des US-amerikanischen Guards Trey Stewart komplettiert der Aufsteiger sein Aufgebot. 🧩 

ℹ️ Der 24-Jährige wechselt von der renommierten Brigham Young University (BYU) aus der NCAA Division I zu den SBB Baskets. 

💬 Eiko Potthast, Cheftrainer der SBB Baskets: „Trey ist ein sehr besonderer Basketballspieler. Es ist sehr besonders, dass er vier Jahre lang am selben College war. Das gibt es heutzutage nicht mehr so häufig. Darüber hinaus ist er ein wahnsinniger Athlet, sehr schnell, sehr große Sprungkraft. Er passt perfekt in unser System. Seine offensive Produktion war in den vergangenen Jahren limitiert, aber wir glauben, dass er das Potenzial hat, uns weiterzuhelfen als zweiter Ballhandler, der mit seiner Athletik offensiv kreieren kann. Am defensiven Ende übernimmt er sehr viel Verantwortung und definiert sein Spiel darüber. Dazu noch ein toller Charakter, also genau das, was wir gesucht haben.“

💬 Kevin Magdowski, Sportlicher Leiter der SBB Baskets: „Wir freuen uns, Trey von solch einem renommierten College verpflichtet zu haben. Er wird uns mit seiner Athletik und seinem Speed vor allem in der Verteidigung die nötige Stabilität geben.“

💬 Trey Stewart, Zugang der SBB Baskets: „Ich kann es kaum erwarten, nach Magdeburg und Wolmirstedt zu kommen und die neue Saison in Angriff zu nehmen. Lasst uns etwas Besonderes schaffen!“

📈 In der vergangenen Saison legte der 1,88 Meter große Guard durchschnittlich 1,7 Punkte und 0,5 Vorlagen pro Partie auf.

caption:
Pillar 2: IDENTITY 

For most of my life, I was known as an athlete. But when that chapter ended, I had to ask who am I without it?

Turns out…a lot!

I’m a sister, daughter, friend, CNA, pre-med student, choreographer, food lover, biology nerd, schedule fanatic, and teacher. I’ve taught hundreds of dancers, been Miss Utah’s Teen, and yes I’ve never had soda and still rewatch dance moms for fun!

That’s what the identity pillar of Win Within is all about! Helping athletes discover who they are beyond the game. Because you’re worth isn’t in your wins. It’s in your values, your voice, and the life you build outside your sport. Let’s help each other know who we are without our sport! 

#winwithin #athlete #athleteidentity #morethanmysport #wholeathlete #missprovo #mentalwellness #purposebeyondperformance

For most of my life, I was known as an athlete. But when that chapter ended, I had to ask who am I without it?

Turns out…a lot!

I’m a sister, daughter, friend, CNA, pre-med student, choreographer, food lover, biology nerd, schedule fanatic, and teacher. I’ve taught hundreds of dancers, been Miss Utah’s Teen, and yes I’ve never had soda and still rewatch dance moms for fun!

That’s what the identity pillar of Win Within is all about! Helping athletes discover who they are beyond the game. Because you’re worth isn’t in your wins. It’s in your values, your voice, and the life you build outside your sport. Let’s help each other know who we are without our sport! 

#winwithin #athlete #athleteidentity #morethanmysport #wholeathlete #missprovo #mentalwellness #purposebeyondperformance

athlete.name: Jared McGregor
athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor with a keen strategic mind, this athlete blends agility and precision on the field. Off the pitch, he’s a thoughtful leader, inspiring teammates with unwavering determination and camaraderie.

caption:
Amid the excitement of BYU’s past campaign where the Cougars reached the Sweet 16, Jared McGregor made an effort to visit ailing individuals the night before almost every game, both at home and on the road. He did this largely on his own and without many of his teammates and coaches knowing, solely wanting to do something he felt was right.

“I just don’t want to leave here feeling like I didn’t make a difference,” McGregor told the Deseret News.

Learn more about McGregor and his "Name of the Game" project at Deseret.com, found at link in bio.

✏️: Jackson Payne, Deseret News
📸: Laura Seitz, Deseret News, Nate Edwards, Jared McGregor

caption:
As I sit in the locker room just finished cleaning it out at Riverside Country Club a wave of emotions hit! It feels like just yesterday I put everything in my locker when I was coming up in the summer to start classes. There are all kinds of emotions like: sadness, loss, tiredness, excitement, wins, happiness, progress, defeat, friendship and so many more. 

There are many hours spend practicing and playing on golf course that have lead me to where I am today! With ending my college golf career there are so many new opportunities and exciting things that are coming my way! 

I will always remember the amazing memories with my team and coaches how they have shaped me into the person I am today. One of my favorite memories is with Coach is when it was just us playing rounds at Riverside in the summers. 

To those still in college sports, just soak in every moment that you have, cause it really does just fly by! 

AD!! ✌🏼⛳️🏌🏻‍♀️

athlete.name: James Corrigan
athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor from a small town, this athlete blends grit with agility. Known for strategic thinking on the field, he inspires teammates with unwavering determination and a contagious passion for the game.

caption:
From humble hustle to steeplechase sensation, James Corrigan is rewriting the script.

Born in Los Angeles and now a force at Brigham Young University, James has quickly made his mark in the 3000-meter steeplechase. In just the past year, he placed third in the U.S. Olympic Trials, secured his Olympic standard in a last-chance race at the Penn Relays, represented Team USA in Paris, and most recently, he became the NCAA Champion with a blistering 8:16 performance.

We’re looking at a mission-serving, faith-centered student of mechanical engineering who has managed to balance it all (Olympic pressure, NCAA podiums, and viral “Sunday Night Live” faith content) while staying grounded and inspiring a generation of young runners.

He juggles, he hurdles, and he races for something bigger.

This is the story of resilience, belief, and barrier-breaking speed.

James Corrigan is in The Running Effect house. And he’s just getting started.

Let’s get into it.

In today’s conversation, James takes me through his NCAA title, his training leading into it, training with Olympic Medalist Kenneth Rooks, his mindset going into USA’s, being married and a dad while in college, and much more. 

This is an inside look into the mind of one of the best runners not just in the NCAA, but in the country. 

Tap into the James Corrigan Special.

athlete.name: Gretchen Hoekstre
athlete.bio: With a fierce determination and a knack for precision, this throws specialist embodies resilience and grit. A natural leader, she inspires teammates through her unwavering work ethic and competitive spirit.

caption:
3x Honorable Mention All- American 
2x All Big 12
BYU school record
2x BYU #2 all time
MPSF champion
More amazing memories and experiences than I can count 

My collegiate athletic career has officially come to an end. My goal for this year was to make it to NCAAs in two events. After 3 could be season ending injuries, one of which 6 weeks before nationals I reached that goal. My forearm finally let up when I was there, but what an amazing opportunity it was to come home and end my career in the very same stadium I started it. caption:
shot for the moon, landed among the stars ⭐️ 

running for BYU was everything i dreamed it would be and more. as time went on, the more i realized that this opportunity was all because of the goodness of God. i don’t know how i got so lucky. 

i know He knows me personally and i’m so grateful i was able to come closer to Him through a sport and a team i love so much. i’ve grown in ways i didn’t know i could, and i know that BYU is where i needed to be. 

this has been the most fun and joyful four years of my life, much thanks to my teammates whom i love. i won’t remember every painful workout or even every great workout, but i’ll always remember how they inspired and supported me day after day. i have achieved so much more with them than i ever could have on my own. i’m so grateful God put every single one of them in my path. 

my biggest takeaway from my track career? i could never doubt God’s love for me.

athlete.name: Trey Stewart
athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor with an infectious smile, this athlete blends strategic acumen and unyielding work ethic. Known for clutch performances, he inspires teammates while navigating the field with deft precision.

caption:
🚬&💵 5 fits for Juneteenth

Earlier this year, my photographer friend George asked me to be part of a Met Gala–inspired project with a Black Dandyism theme. It was incredible and really gave me a creative push to try something new. It made me think about how I express myself through the fit and fabric selections in my clothing—I’ve always wanted to be unapologetically me, even in spaces where that’s hard.

Nicer events it was hard for me to still dress how I feel comfortable while keeping the code. Church is about worship, but I still want to feel like myself. Find a balance of me and respect. Tailored looks are personal to everyone—for me, that means baggy. I started sewing and altering clothes so I could show up as me while praising God and His Son.

These looks also carry heavy Civil Rights themes. In all the patterns are symbolism. Studying that history has shaped my art and given it deeper meaning. In high school, I was often the only Black kid. Hearing All-Amerikkkan Bada$$ made me start exploring my Black identity, and that flag bag represents the beginning of that journey.

Judas and the Black Messiah was a big influence, but the film Sinners inspired this project the most. Its subtle styling differences between characters said so much—I tried to do the same. 

I love West Coast fashion, but East Coast, especially New York, will always be number one for me. I blended both here, but kept NY on top. It’s all in the details and I was proud of how all this turned out. 

Materials: @silhouette.inc gave me a new machine that allowed me to try out some new designs and methods especially with the size of the cuts you can do. @designcofabrics always inspires me with the best fabrics.

Photographer: @georgengatuvai the man’s work is incredible. Thank you brother for the inspiration.

athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor with a fierce love for the game, she combines agility and strategic finesse, often outsmarting opponents. Off the field, her infectious enthusiasm inspires teammates and fans alike.

caption:
•••••
Running can be complicated. Some performances leave you on cloud nine while others leave you utterly disappointed.
This weekend was definitely one that made me ask myself: Am I good enough to make my dreams a reality in this sport? And while the race this weekend didn’t end the way I wanted, I know I am capable. Excited to keep learning, keep the faith, and keep giving it my all because I truly love this sport. I believe in myself, and I’m lucky to have a support system that also believes in me and my potential.
•••••
A dream delayed isn’t a dream denied. One of these times, it’ll all come together. Grateful for another chance to line up for a NCAA final and make so many amazing memories this weekend.
•••••
#BYUrun4her #Nike #5k #ontothenextone

athlete.name: Eliza White
athlete.bio: A tenacious distance runner with a passion for perseverance, she thrives on long runs through breathtaking landscapes, blending grit with grace. Her infectious enthusiasm fuels teammates, inspiring all around her.

caption:
God is so good. 

I’m so so grateful for this past year at BYU! So many lifelong friendships have been made and memories that will last forever. 

This years’ xc/track season didn’t go as I expected or hoped for, but i wouldn’t trade it for the world. My injuries and setbacks have taught me so much and given me the opportunity to grow in so many ways. 

The last couple months I’ve had a lot of self-reflection and incredible personal experiences that have led me to make the decision to serve a mission for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints. It was not an easy decision, but ultimately is what the Lord has in store for me and my life. It’s hard to put my life on hold and leave BYU, my teammates and the incredible experience it has been of being a part of the BYU sisterhood 💙

But I know that the next 18 months of my life that I will be serving in McAllen, Texas speaking Spanish, will be such a blessing for me. 

I’m excited to serve the Lord and the dedicate this time of my life to sharing the good news of the Gospel of Jesus Christ 🤍 September 2025-March 2027. 

I’m so grateful to my coach for this amazing year, the opportunity she has given me, and her love and support in my decision. 

To my incredible teammates who I love so much and will be forever grateful for their friendship, memories we’ve made, and for their amazing examples. 

For my roommates who are amazing in every way and make life so sweet.

I’ll be back, and can’t wait to continue chasing my dreams with the people I love so much! #byurun4her #byutrackfieldxc

Coach Spotlight #1 - Jefferson McMullin

Jefferson is the founder and head coach of On-Tempo Performance. He is from Lehi, UT and is currently a member of the BYU Cross Country and Track teams. Before BYU, he ran cross country and track for Lehi High School where he was a state champion in both cross country and the 800m and 1600m events. He also won the NXR Southwest XC Championship. After finishing high school, he served a mission for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Uruguay.

Jefferson is currently studying exercise science at BYU with plans of becoming a physical therapist. Outside of running, Jefferson enjoys mountain biking, spikeball, traveling and all things Star Wars.

athlete.name: Cole Ponich
athlete.bio: Hailing from a rich wrestling heritage, this tenacious athlete blends agility with strategic finesse, often outmaneuvering opponents with clever tactics. Off the mat, his infectious enthusiasm uplifts teammates, fostering camaraderie.

caption:
7 years ago I made the decision to stay at home and come play golf at BYU. Growing up I can’t say I ever saw myself wearing the Y but they say some of the best things in life are unexpected and looking back on my time here I couldn’t agree more. 

This place is truly special and will forever be a huge part of my life. There’s nothing like playing for a program that genuinely has your best interest and wants to help you achieve your goals in any way they can. I could never thank all the people that I was surrounded by enough for the amount of effort they put into helping me succeed on and off the golf course.

It hasn’t always been smooth sailing for me. Those that know me know that I went through some things that really set me back and at times I didn’t know if I’d ever find my way out of it. To my coaches….you guys had every reason to give up on me and you never stopped believing and for that I will forever be grateful, you guys will always be family to me. 

To my teammates…we’ll always be a part of making history at BYU. First ever team to win a regional and first ever team to have a chance to make match play at the ncaa championships. More then anything, Im going to miss all the times we’re on the road competing together doing what we all love most and making memories that I’ll never forget. Love you guys like brothers and can’t wait to see what the future holds for each of us. 

I believe it’s not how you start, but how you finish and I’ll always be able to hold my head high knowing I gave it everything I had this year to help make this team great. 

Once a coug always a coug 💙🤙🏼 

If you ever stopped believing in me don’t start again now…On to the next chapter

athlete.name: Simon Kwon
athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor with a keen strategic mind, this athlete blends skillful finesse with relentless determination. Hailing from a rich cultural background, he embodies resilience and teamwork, inspiring those around him.

caption:
Great moments are born from great opportunity.

This loss has been hard to swallow. We had a chance at a National Championship and came up short. Many people have congratulated us and talked about how we made history at BYU, but at the end of the day, we lost. I will remember this feeling for the rest of my life, and it will only make me a better person because of it. Dealing with loss is a part of life, one we can’t escape, and I am so grateful for the opportunity to learn and grow. All of the challenges I have faced have made me the person I am today.

In moments of disappointment, we discover who we truly are. The pain of this loss will only fuel me to work harder and become stronger. I promise to give everything I have to this team and to this university.

I love this team, and I am so grateful to represent @brighamyounguniversity. I wouldn’t trade this journey for anything, and I look forward to what the future holds for all of us.

With this being my first real tournament going against amazing anglers i would say we did pretty good. the first day we were leading the lady bracket and overall 44th. then on sunday the conditions changed and made it super tough for us to get the bites we got the day before. we caught so many fish this weekend just not any big ones like others and couldn’t adapt to the weather switch up. overall though we learned a lot and ended up getting 59th. for this being my first tournament and tae’s first as well i’d say we did good enough. came home with a brand new nrx rod from the raffles. amazing weekend with amazing people. gonna hop into a few summer circuits and see if we can place better next time. thanks hunny for sticking it out even though we were cold and wet and spearing waves all day. i love you ❤️

We’re beyond excited to welcome Justin back to Utah, where his family, roots, and heart have always been.

Justin and his incredible wife bring more than talent—they bring character, humility, and a heart for the game and community. We’re grateful to be part of this next chapter and honored our team could help bring him back home where he belongs.

Here’s to family, faith, and football. Let’s go to work!

caption:
ENJOY > ENDURE 

That’s the lesson I’ve been learning recently. 

To expound, there’s two ways to experience the same thing. Heading into Easter, we read an example of this when Christ was suffering on the cross:

He had two robbers next to Him. They both were suffering through the same thing, but experiencing it in different ways…
1. One felt hopeless as he doubted Christ for not using His power to save them in that moment. 
2. The other felt hopeful knowing that Christ would use His power to save him in the kingdom of God one day. 

We can choose to find hope and peace in Christ as we experience our own growth opportunities. I hope all can ENJOY their opportunities rather than ENDURE them!

caption:
Thought I’d post now that my medical redshirt season is almost officially over!! Where do I start? It has been the slowest yet fastest seven months of my life! From the beginning, I knew it wasn’t going to be easy because of my past experience with this injury. But fortunately and unfortunately, due to my brain’s trauma response, I forgot everything I went through during my first two ACL recoveries—lol. That being said, I am so much more proud of my 13- and 14-year-old self for enduring this injury twice at such a young age!

I want to talk about the importance of my mental journey throughout the past six to seven months. Multiple people have asked me, “Are you still going to do gym?” and my answer has simply been, “Why not?” But recently, while self-reflecting, I realized I need to focus on finding the reasons why instead of just why not? And oh boy, do I have endless reasons why this sport is worth it for me!

First and foremost, gymnastics brings me so much closer to my Heavenly Father. One instance was during the first couple of months when I struggled to get full extension (straightening) in my knee. In the depths of my struggles, I decided to fast on Fast Sunday for help with my extension. The week following my knee made a huge improvement! I learned that when I need help I can ask anyone whether it is from someone in my life on earth or my Heavenly Father! 
My second reason—one of many—is that gymnastics, and especially this injury, has given me the opportunity to spend more time with my family. After my niece Lily passed away last year, family became my only priority in life. Unfortunately, living in Utah and spending so much time in the gym made it hard to get the quality time with them that I longed for. After I hurt my knee, I had doctor’s appointments in Arizona every two weeks. This gave me the chance to get the much-needed quality time with my family. In the moment, I questioned why I was going through so much physical pain, but looking back now, I realize it was exactly what I needed to heal mentally after losing Lily. (Currently happy/proud crying while writing this.) 
Continued in comments…

caption:
WHAT I WANT

I want food. I want sleep. I want to be held. I want food. I want sleep. I want up. I want down. I can’t make up my mind. I want sleep.

I want a toy. I want to break it. I want a new one. I want to walk. I want to do it by myself. I want a cookie. I want to stay up. I want to run. I want sleep.

I want to play games. I want to win. I want friends. I want to be smart. I want people to like me. I want to be better than them. I want to go home. I want my homework to go away. I want it to be easier.

I want to be happy. I want a best friend. I want to know if God is there. I want to feel good. I want to stop making mistakes. I want it to be easier. I want to be successful. I want to feel good about who I am. I want God to be there.

⋅⋅

I want forgiveness. I want to feel God near me. I want to know more about Him. I want to make my family proud. I want to be a good person. I want to change myself. I can’t change myself. I want God to help me. I want to know Him.

I want God to be proud of me. I want to show him my gratitude for what He has done for me. I want a family of my own. I want everyone to know about Jesus. I want the people who already know about Him to connect even deeper. I want God to continue to change my heart. I want what He wants. I want God to be able to look at my life and then say, “I can tell that you truly loved me.”

La mediofondista ecuatoriana Carmen Alder, quien compite para la Brigham Young University de Utah (EE.UU.), batió el récord sudamericano de la milla en pista cubierta al ganar esa prueba en el torneo Harvard Invitational, en Cambridge. Alder marcó 4:29.49, mejorando los 4:34.37 que había conseguido el 27 de enero del año apsado en Boston.

Alder también posee el récord sudamericano de los 5.000 metros en pista cubierta con 15:51.98 y, además, las marcas «indoor» de su país en 800 (2:10.13), 1.000 (2:47.49) y 3.000 (9:03.71

Felicitaciones!!! 🇪🇨🇪🇨💯

caption:
1️⃣ year post op!! I am so grateful to be back and doing the sport I love most. you never know when it will be taken away from you, and every moment spent doing something you love is special. I am blessed to be a part of such an amazing team like @byugymnastics 💙

I couldn’t have done this without the support from my family, friends and teammates who pushed me to be better every day. I knew I could count on them when I didn’t want to smile or when I didn’t have the motivation to do a lot of things. I am so grateful to have such an amazing support system in my life. 

Thank you to the best PT’s a girl could ask for @sportsptmidkiff_fit and @philliphartog !! you guys pushed me to better myself physically and mentally. there is nothing that I could do to ever pay you back for the work you have put into me to make me 100% again. 

It is crazy to see all of the progress and work put into this recovery. this wasn’t easy but I am grateful to continue my gymnastics journey. this was God’s plan for me and I am super glad to be able to have learned so many lessons and become a better version of myself!! 

GO COUGS 💙🤙🏻

There will be times when we feel discouraged, beaten down, and overwhelmed by life and the challenges that come with it. As we turn to and rely on Jesus Christ, we can feel His love and be comforted, as well as receive the strength we need to overcome or make it through any trial we face.🤍

caption:
“Awe” is an experience that is unique to human existence. Scenes in nature like these are awe-inspiring to me. Music also inspires awe for me, as I’m one of those people that gets chills and teary eyed even listening to certain songs with no lyrics.

There are many people who have faith in a higher being, but I wonder how many of us feel this sense of awe and wonder towards our experiences with God?

When has God inspired awe in us? How often do we just sit in awe and WONDER at who He really is? Do we truly “stand all amazed”?

If we aren’t in awe of God and his magnificent plan, and his tender mercies in our lives, then it’s just because we don’t understand it. 

If the gospel of Christ doesn’t seem too good to be true, then I don’t think we get it yet :)

caption: i've been home from my mission now for a little while but i wanted to share about my experience there. it was the best decision i've ever made but probably also the hardest. i've never been surrounded a more humble, faithful group of people. i saw both many struggles & many miracles. i've come to learn that God is a god of miracles & of love. He puts us in positions to test our potential because He loves us & He knows exactly what we can become. i'm so grateful for all the people i got to meet & the friends i made. there are many people i'll never forget for their kindness or the lessons they taught me. i know i was supposed to teach them but they taught me so much more. i also felt what true joy is. like Elder Patrick Kearon said, "we are members of the church of joy!" we can experience so much joy despite our life circumstances. i met so many genuinely happy people that maybe didn't have much, but they knew what was most important. i'm grateful for the gospel & the joy it brings into my life & the lives of so many people. & more than anything, im grateful for my Savior. He is the reason we can truly feel joy in this life & after 🫶🏼

athlete.name: Jacob Stanford
athlete.bio: A strategic thinker on the field, this athlete blends tenacity with finesse, showcasing a relentless pursuit of excellence. Off the pitch, a charismatic leader, inspiring teammates with unwavering positivity and camaraderie.

caption:
BYU Cross Country - NCAA D1 National Champions 2024

My heart is brimming with pride and joy for this team of epic proportions! This was an achievement that many dismissed as impossible. It’s quite fortunate to have the season of gratitude to conclude every cross country season, and I would like to share what I am especially grateful for right now.

I’m thankful for God and His call to be a Disciple of Jesus Christ, even in a field as temporal as athletics.

I’m thankful for my coaches and athletic trainers who have shown me patience and made me feel seen and heard even through a season of ups and downs. I think it’s fair to say that we have some of if not the most talented, experienced coaches and staff on the planet!

I’m thankful for my family and my lovely girlfriend Xela for always being supportive and making cross country one of their passions simply because they care about me.

I’m thankful for my teammates, my brothers! I love these guys more than words can describe. Each has a story of overcoming impossible odds to be the incredible man that they are. They are daily examples of what it means to be a dedicated athlete, Olympian, husband, (soon father!), scholar, and Christian. It’s been my honor to train and compete with them this season.

Lastly, almost strangely, I’m thankful for my trials. Sicknesses and injuries have taught me that nothing, even fitness from hard work, can be taken for granted. Fortunately this year, none of these came at the cost of the national title, but these trials show me where I can improve and be even more disciplined in the future.

Speaking of the future, it’s bright like always. BYU has a way of finding guys to rise up when it’s needed. You can trust and believe in BYU XC for years to come!

Thank you.

#byu #byuxc #byucrosscountry #ncaa #ncaacrosscountry #ncaatf #nationalchampionship #nattychamps #crosscountry #xc

athlete.name: Hunter Kitchen
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a sharp basketball IQ, this versatile guard thrives on court vision and strategic play. Off the hardwood, his infectious enthusiasm inspires teammates and electrifies fans alike.

caption:
This cross country season didn’t go quite as I expected, but that doesn’t mean I haven’t seen God’s hand in my life through it all. From not being able to walk after rupturing my plantar fascia in a race (where I thought the season was all over) to running in a national championship just six weeks later, it’s been a journey. At first, things weren’t looking good with problem after problem coming up as I tried to recover. Even with all of this, I don’t know why, but I feel beyond blessed. It’s amazing to see how everything came together during that time. “And because he hath done this, my beloved brethren, have miracles ceased? Behold I say unto you, Nay; neither have angels ceased to minister unto the children of men.” (Moroni 7:29)

I spent hours on the bike, on the elliptical, and in the pool, trying to regain the fitness I’d lost from not running. All of this was for just a slim chance of being able to compete by the time the big race came around.

It’s truly a miracle how fast my foot was able to heal. Talking to friends who had the same injury really put it into perspective. By a miracle, my recovery time was just a fraction of what I thought it would be.

I have the best friends, family, teammates, and coaches. I can’t express how grateful I am for all of them, especially Coach Wood and @saltlakexctf . The opportunities I’ve been given are far more than I deserve, and I can’t believe this season is already over. God is real.

📸: @cgphoto_media

athlete.bio: An agile powerhouse, this all-around star blends artistry and precision in every routine. With a fierce determination and a contagious smile, she inspires teammates while captivating audiences across the mat.

caption:
Third times the charm! (but the right knee this time) 
A few weeks ago I was in practice and I took one turn that flipped my world upside down once again. For those who don’t know me super well, I tore my left acl in 8th grade and again in 9th grade. So due to my past I almost immediately knew I had torn my acl and for this to happen on my opposite leg 6 years later is pretty out of the blue! The past few weeks I had struggled wondering why Heavenly Father would put this setback in my plan knowing how traumatic it was to me.

Last week I opened my scriptures to a random page and I read John 13:7. The verse said, “Jesus answered and said unto him, What I do thou knowest not now; but thou shalt know hereafter.” I was filled with feelings of peace and reassurance after reading that scripture. It helped me realize that our heavenly father has a plan for me. Even though my year isn’t going to go how I planned, I know that I can trust in the lords timing and what he has in store for me! Excited for the future and the comeback starts now!! 💙💙

athlete.name: Tanner Edwards
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a fierce spirit, this swimmer glides through the water with grace and precision. Balancing technique and tenacity, he embodies the essence of teamwork and perseverance.

caption:
Well this is not exactly what I planned but last Saturday during our first meet in Colorado during my 50 butterfly, on my last stroke I felt a “pop” in my shoulder. Went to the doctors and got an MRI and it showed my labrum was torn. In a couple weeks I will be getting surgery which will end my season. I can’t tell you how much this stinks and how upset I am but I have just felt peace the entire week. I know God has a perfect plan for me. There is a quote I love by Elder Mark Bragg that has been going through my mind:

 “Of course, the Savior is the ultimate example of poise. In the Garden of Gethsemane, in unimaginable agony, as “he sweat as it were great drops of blood,” He exemplified divine poise with the simple yet majestic statement “Not my will, but thine, be done.”

I have no idea why this is happening but I try to look to the example of my Savior and say, “not my will but thine be done.” I know God is in the details and He is with me every step of the way. I’m excited for the next couple of months and ready to get back after it! All Heart❤️

caption: I’m very excited to announce that I have committed to continue my volleyball career playing D1 volleyball at Brigham Young University! Since I was a kid, volleyball has been in the center of my life. I’ve fallen in love with the sport and it has been my support for my whole life. Watching my dad and grandpa coach and play I always strived to be just like them. Some of the greatest moments in my life have come from volleyball and I’m so glad that I can continue to work on myself and my game through them. I would like to thank all coaches that have helped along the way and grew me to be the player I am. I would like to thank my family and especially parents for believing in me and being on my sidelines the whole time through thick and thin! Thank you to @clubgsl for letting me develop to be great! Thank you to my friends for being my #1 supporters and help me grow as a person. Finally I would like to thank god and our savior for helping me through all trials and making me a better person each day. #gocougs #volleyball @byumvolleyball @olmiefam @farraholmstead

caption:
To our gamers, fans, and friends,

We would like to humbly thank all of those who supported the development, launch, and success of the Hay Bales games!

What started as a small passion project in the summer of 2016 evolved into an expansive universe- in which we wanted to capture the light of the unique personalities of our childhood. It was a monument to our friends and a time capsule for ourselves.

The success of Hay Bales 3 was shocking- we reached the Top Charts of the AppStore in less than 24 hours of release! It was a dream come true after years of development.

Unfortunately, this era of our life was never going to last forever- and we regret to inform you that in the coming days Hay Bales will no longer be available to download on the AppStore.

On the bright side, this means that we as developers and businessmen are moving on to more expansive, professional products, apps that will change the way you interact with your smartphone, and in turn, the world. We are just getting started with what we can create!

If you want to have Hay Bales 3 one last time, please go download it and enjoy it for free! We will never forget this huge stepping stone for our personal growth and experience.

MASSIVE projects are currently in the works. Please stay tuned!

No matter how professional our products become, we always want our “handmade” approach to exist in our apps. We hope you can feel the passion behind each pixel in what we create.

Thank you.
The Stanford Twins

caption:
#GodisGood 

A few weeks ago, I had an interaction with a little girl and she was wearing a bracelet that said “God is Good.” She had told me her friend made it for her and she wore it because she liked the color of it lol. Those simple words on that bracelet had a big impact on me. There is so much good on this Earth and God wants us to enjoy it! My dad has always said the church is simple and since getting older I have finally understood how true that is. “The Gospel of Jesus Christ is simple, no matter how much we try to complicate it. We should strive to keep our lives similarly simple, unencumbered by extraneous influences, focused on those things that matter most.” -Elder Ballard 

Me+ @sadikelley + @brooklyn.easton went to a few different temples yesterday and the goodness and simplicity that comes from being in the temple is incredible. God is the greatest and I am so grateful to be living in a place where I can attend the temple whenever! 😊
