athlete.name: James Corrigan
athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor from a small town, this athlete blends grit with agility. Known for strategic thinking on the field, he inspires teammates with unwavering determination and a contagious passion for the game.

caption:
THANK YOU FOR CHEERING ONE MORE TIME! We really did it. This last Saturday I ran 8:13 to secure my spot for the Olympic Team. Here’s some awesome stats and then some of my thoughts
✅Another 8 second PR
✅Olympic Standard
✅Facility Record 
✅School Record 
✅American Collegiate Record
✅Ticket Punched to Paris 2024
 
How can you ask for more? After a stellar Olympic Trials Final race I was left with a situation where I needed to run a fast enough time or accrue enough World Ranking Points to secure my spot. My coaches, agent and friends rushed to help figure out how we could make this a possibility. I’m so grateful to Aaron Robison for helping us and including us in the Penn Relays summer showcase. We couldn’t have done it without him. I also want to thank Dan Michalski who came to pace and did a stellar job. With so much support this race also led to immense pressure to perform. Not only for my own sake but to make the provisions worth it. As I showed up to the track on the day of the race, my heart went out to those who had flown across the country to support, to families who drove several hours from their home state to be with me and to local track fans who wanted to witness a piece of history for themselves. I’m glad I was able to share this awesome experience with everyone. 
When the gun went off I just focused on following Dan. As he brought me through a mile I told myself silently, “You’re going to the Olympics.” When I saw the time with 800 to go I was elated. With a lap to go I visibly smiled as Kenny yelled at me what I needed to close in. I knew I was going to do it. Flying down the homestretch I’ve never felt or heard a louder crowd and it made crossing the line the greatest feeling. 

3 races 
8 days 
I’m going to the Olympics 

Thank you to my family friends and coaches, I can’t wait to represent the USA at the Olympics. I will do my best to respond to everyone in due time. See you in Paris! 
📸: @just_in_time215 
#olympics #olympian #trackandfield #steeplechase #byu #usa

caption:
Tanner Edwards-

“In this confusing world, I testify that Jesus Christ is the only way to find true and lasting peace. I know He lives and loves us. His gospel is the way to unlock His help more fully in this life. Everything He ask us to do, is to come closer to Him and to help us overcome this crazy world. I know the Book of Mormon is the true word of God, and the pages are filled with the teachings of Jesus Christ. I testify along side the Prophet Joseph Smith, “that the Book of Mormon was the most correct of any book on earth, and the keystone of our religion, and a man would get nearer to God by abiding by its precepts, than by any other book.” I know because of Christ Atonement, you can not only be forgiven for your sins, but you can be transformed. He lives, He knows you and He is looking for every opportunity to help you!”

Served a mission in Portland, Oregon

All Big-12 1st team
NCAA qualifier

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with an unyielding spirit, this distance runner thrives on pushing boundaries. Fueled by passion and resilience, she embodies dedication, inspiring teammates with her unwavering focus and infectious enthusiasm.

caption:
My US Olympian🇺🇸❤️

I’ve been thinking a lot about dreams lately. 

What it means to set them and give everything to reach that one thing. 

Are dreams worth it? Is it worth the anxiety, stress, sleepless nights, endless sacrifices, uncomfortably, tears, and potential failure? 

Isn’t it easier to stick to a path that’s stable, guarantees success, keeps us emotionally, physically, and spiritually at equilibrium, and that requires low stress? 

My answer? It IS easier to just stay within your comfortable bubble. Problem is, you don’t grow that way. 

If there’s anything Conner’s taught me since I met him, is to give everything I have to the path I’m on. 

Conner helped me give my all on my mission, to my family, and now to my degree.

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a knack for breaking tackles, this powerhouse blends agility and power. Off the field, his infectious enthusiasm and leadership inspire teammates, embodying the spirit of BYU football.

caption:
After finishing my mission, I was told that I’d climbed to the top of a mountain to see that there’s a larger mountain in the distance.

Now that I go to BYU, and am surrounded by mountains, I’ve been thinking a lot about what it means to climb mountains in our personal lives: whether of desires we have, goals, or adversity we face.

To anyone currently climbing or seeing a large mountain to climb, here’s some words that have given me faith and hope, from President Russell M. Nelson (“Christ is risen, faith in Him will move mountains”).
…
“If we “have faith as a grain of mustard seed,” we shall be able to “say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto [us].”
…
Start today to increase your faith. Through your faith, Jesus Christ will increase your ability to move the mountains in your life, even though your personal challenges may loom as large as Mount Everest.
…
He took upon Himself your misery, your mistakes, your weakness, and your sins. He paid the compensatory price and provided the power for you to move every mountain you will ever face. You obtain that power with your faith, trust, and willingness to follow Him. The Savior is never closer to you than when you are facing or climbing a mountain with faith.
…
Moving your mountains may require a miracle. Learn about miracles. Miracles come according to your faith in the Lord. Central to that faith is trusting His will and timetable—how and when He will bless you with the miraculous help you desire. Only your unbelief will keep God from blessing you with miracles to move the mountains in your life.
…
Your growing faith in Him will move mountains—not the mountains of rock that beautify the earth but the mountains of misery in your lives. Your flourishing faith will help you turn challenges into unparalleled growth and opportunity.”

athlete.name: Ellie Boyer
athlete.bio: A fierce competitor with a passion for the water, this Butterfly and Individual Medley specialist combines grace and tenacity. Known for her infectious enthusiasm, she inspires teammates while striving for excellence.

caption:
Wednesday night, my precious little sister lost her life in a terrible accident. Oh Shaela how we all love you so much. One of my favorite memories were when we’d go to the ocean. No matter where we were, she would always run straight in and start playing. Me having the huge fear of the ocean would always sit in awe of how fearless she was. She was just so brave and fierce in everything she did. She would then always come back to shore and say “Ellie stop being a scaredy cat and come play!” While holding my hand, she would always get me to go out with her. Her giggling about my little shrieks all while holding my hand would let me know that she would keep me safe. No one could get me to push past my fears like she did. So effortlessly fearless and strong.
Out of the bottom of my heart, I know that this isn’t the end. My sister would want each of us to live just like she did. Fearless. I’m grateful to know that my family can and will live on forever through God’s perfect plan. ShaeShae will always be the biggest light and blessing to my family. We will always love you so infinitely Shae and you made a forever blessing to us. Go shred up some more waves and soccer fields up in heaven. I already know she will have closets full of Nikes. 
From me and my family, we are so grateful for the many prayers and comforts each of you have sent us at this time. We are so blessed to have so many people we know love us. We sure do love you all. At this time, I invite each of you to always #playlikeshaeshae #16 ❤️💙

Last summer, I was blessed to have the opportunity to serve alongside Tyler during one of the final weeks of my mission. Today, we dropped him off at the airport for the beginning of his mission experience. 

Tyler is a light and a great example to all who have been blessed to know him. When we served together in Portland, he never hesitated when presented with an opportunity to bear testimony of the Savior and his doctrine. Following his time in Oregon, after a long process of prayer and fasting, he decided to serve a mission of his own - assigned to Buenos Aires, Argentina. 

“they separated themselves and departed one from another, trusting in the Lord that they should meet again at the close of their harvest; for they supposed that great was the work which they had undertaken.”

Although I already miss him greatly, I couldn’t be more happy and proud. It truly is a special day for him and our family!

athlete.name: Ethan Thomason
athlete.bio: A mountain of strength, this offensive lineman blends tenacity with precision, protecting his quarterback like a fortress. Known for his relentless work ethic, he embodies teamwork and resilience on and off the field.

caption:
Tomorrow I get to take my little sister Kirsten and cousin James to a BYU game for her 14th birthday.

It’s going to be cool as always but also sad. The last time I spent time with my cousin Dexton who died, was at a game. He was only 14. I wish he would have told me in all the times we talked or texted he was hurting. Maybe I should have known. I was 14 once and it was hard. I had very low confidence and was sad and felt alone a lot. I hid behind a smile. Ages 12-18 can be a very hard time for many kids and for me that is definitely true. I know for me I wish I was able to intervene and let him know that life gets so much better! I wish so badly I could have helped keep him and I'm sure that everyone who misses him feels the same. 
 
If you know someone who is struggling please talk to them. You might have to ask a lot of questions; don't let an “I’m fine” brush you off. 
 
I hope we all can be a lot braver about helping each other. We mess around and act like life is easy… it’s not. We post pics of the highlights of our lives and that can be fun but it’s not the truth. A lot of the time life is very hard and not glamorous. EVERYONE has hard times no matter how sensationalized life seems for them and it is important to remember that. I no longer have the chance to try to help Dexton now but we are trying to find some purpose in this to help spread awareness of suicide and remind people to have the courage to help. 
Everyone is fighting battles that we don't know about. I love you Dexton. You were nothing but love and kindness. You are so missed and loved. If you are able and want to help his family please donate to the Go Fund Me in my bio. 💜💜
